2609.29766.title: Anatomy-aware cross-speaker adaptation of complete vocal-tract acoustic-to-articulatory inversion
2609.29766.paper_summary: Cross-speaker acoustic-to-articulatory inversion requires accounting for anatomical differences between speakers. We propose a geometric adaptation framework that uses anatomical landmarks, primarily on vertebrae and dental structures,to transfer predictions from a fixed inversion model to unseen speakers. An affine transformation followed by thin-plate spline (TPS) deformation maps the predicted contours of 10 vocal-tract structures into each target speaker's geometry without retraining. Landmarks are identified in one selected /u/ frame per speaker as a common phonetic reference without assuming identical articulatory configurations across speakers, and the resulting mapping is reused across recordings. We train the model on a single-speaker rt-MRI database and evaluate adaptation on eight speakers from a separate multi-speaker rt-MRI database. We compare affine and TPS configurations using 12 or 14 landmarks. Affine12+TPS14 achieves the lowest mean point-to-closest-point error of 3.19mm. These results support the combined value of anatomical landmark information and nonrigid alignment.
2609.29766.paper_summary_zh: 跨說話者的聲學到發音反演需要考慮說話者之間的解剖差異。<lb/>我們提出了一個幾何適應框架，利用解剖標誌，主要集中在脊椎和牙齒結構上，將固定反演模型的預測轉移到未見過的說話者。<lb/>一個仿射變換隨後進行薄板樣條（TPS）變形，將10個聲道結構的預測輪廓映射到每個目標說話者的幾何形狀中，而無需重新訓練。<lb/>在每個說話者中選擇一個 /u/ 框架來識別標誌，作為共同的語音參考，而不假設說話者之間的發音配置相同，並且所得到的映射在錄音中重複使用。<lb/>我們在單一說話者的 rt-MRI 數據庫上訓練模型，並在來自另一個多說話者的 rt-MRI 數據庫的八個說話者上評估適應性。<lb/>我們使用12或14個標誌比較仿射和TPS配置。<lb/>Affine12+TPS14達到了最低的平均點到最近點誤差3.19mm。<lb/>這些結果支持了解剖標誌信息和非剛性對齊的結合價值。
